where: 2.14.4 'the player is paid x − y through the one earn'; 9.2 rules-money 'money.ts (bankSplit inside earn)'; 10 hook 1; 2.3.3 'AwayCard.net'
problem: earn is not in money.ts. It is called after the ticket is printed, so the ticket cannot print y. A split inside earn would also split ad rewards and granted scrip unless they bypass earn, and if they bypass it they also miss the income buckets (the advice budget) and the away card's money: the spec says neither. AwayCard.net (the I gate's measure) is not defined once a bank share exists.
evidence: clock.ts:128 earn(x, amount, t); round.ts:104-106 printTicket then earn; deal.ts:80-82 earn then printTicket; advice.ts:216 budget = cash + minutes × incomeRate.
change: Add bank.ts payLot(x, gross, t): {y, z}, called at the five sites of 2.14.4 BEFORE printTicket (the ticket carries bank.y); it then calls earn(x, z, t). Add clock.ts credit(x, a, t, kind: 'ad' | 'grant'), which adds to cash and x.earned only, not to the income buckets or away.money. AwayCard gains bank; net stays money − spent (gross of the bank) and is the I gate's measure; the away bonus's base is money − bank.
ruling: do: bank.ts payLot(x, gross, t) is called at the lot payments BEFORE the ticket prints and then calls earn with the player's part; a separate credit() for ad rewards and granted scrip (cash and earned only: never the income buckets, never a payment the bank shares in); the away card gains the bank's take; the away bonus is half of what reached the player.

where: 2.15.4 'stores pending {product, S, I, at} (one per product)'; 2.15.5; grantProduct(id, txId, quote)
problem: One pending quote per product can grant an amount other than the one shown, and a kill at the wrong moment loses a paid pack.

where: 2.8.1 'A rate plate draws from every bay whose route names it, by the cumulative rule'; 'a hall is charged by Take from bays ... as the crucible is'

where: 2.3.2 'read I when their card opens ... and keep it'; 2.14.3 'computed when the card opens, I frozen there'; 4.3 'I frozen at opening'

where: 2.3.1 step 3 'R_bind = min over steps of capacity ÷ that share'

where: 2.20 'reconcileSalvage accepts layouts 2 and 3 ... lots.nextAt = now + period ... At rung 3 the works layer opens with the bath at the first tick'

The works layer and the bath are derived from rung ≥ 3 plus an absent counts.bathSet, not from the rung event. forCrucible_g maps to reserved.crucible. Test: a layout-2 rung-3 save gets the bath at its first tick.

where: 2.12 'While he is in the yard a tagged thing is his: he racks it or cuts it'

where: 2.3.1 step 1 ("each open partner's L skips over max(fill_s, the trip time ÷ the trucks that serve it)") and step 2 ("the trucks")
problem: I gives the whole truck to every partner, as the built ratedOf does, and its trip time leaves out the hook, weigh and tip phases. I, and every number priced in hours of I, comes out about twice too high, so the 0.9-1.1 gate cannot pass.
evidence: rate.ts 41-47 sums each partner's supply on its own. REPORT6 F3 gives R 82.1 t/h at minute 60, while the bench's six hours moved 232 loads (about 93 s a load, 27-46 t/h by skip mass) plus the drop-off. The formula's trip is 43 s to the farm and 66 s to the demolition site. With four partners at rung 3 the overcount grows.
change: Write the trucks as a time budget: loads an hour = min(Σ_p 3600·L_p/fill_p, 3600·trucks/t̄_trip). t̄_trip is the mix-weighted planned trip of 2.1.2, the same seven-phase function the driver's run plans. Allocate loads to partners highest net margin a load first. ratedOf keeps its form for the ceilings only.
ruling: do, as the lead's I2 and I3 (notes/engine2-LEAD.md).

where: 2.3.1 step 4 ("at its LOWEST margin"), 2.7.1 ("I counts the lower-margin route"; "default the plate bought last"), 2.8 induction hall ("For I: the lower-margin recipe"); ruling 10.6
problem: The lowest-margin rule cannot coexist with the gate in 2.3.3 or with the payback prices in 2.6.4. I runs far below away income whenever the yard runs the better route or recipe, and plates that share an input are priced on the worse margin. If 'bay' counts as a route, every routed plate's ΔI is 0.
evidence: Light iron at 8 t/h with the baler and shredder plus eddy current owned: I counts the baler, 8,000 × 0.12 = §960/h, while the yard on the shredder earns 8,000 × (1.43 − 0.50) = §7,440/h, a shortfall of §6,480/h. Induction hall on bronze at 500 kg/h: brass margin §3.83/kg against bronze §11.79/kg, a shortfall of §3,980/h. Either alone uses up most of a ±10 % band.
change: I never reads routes or recipes as set. It assigns each source flow to the owned plates' capacity, highest margin per kg first (one greedy pass), and uses 'bay' only for what no plate takes. Switching then cannot raise I because I does not read the switch, which keeps the purpose of ruling 10.6. A bay's default route is the same allocation, not 'the plate bought last'.

where: 2.3.3 gate ("AwayCard.net ÷ the hours the yard ran"), 2.22 row I, 8.2; also 2.3.1 step 5
problem: The thing the gate compares against swings by more than its band for reasons that have nothing to do with I. Separately, I double-counts the Yard sale and the van and ignores reagents.
evidence: AwayCard.net = money − spent (types.ts 1064) is taken at the posted step, with x up to ±0.06. Net is a difference of gross: 1,757 against 700 a minute played, gross/net about 2 to 4 on the bench, so a ±3 % step moves net 8-12 %. It is also after the bank's share: 0.2 × gross is a half to nine tenths of net while an agreement is open. It is not corrected for stock change (held bays, `unsold`). In I, the rack's whole gate value is added although its scrap value (40 %, §977/h at the §2,443/h ceiling) is already in m̄. Reagents (0.015 and 0.02 a kg) are not subtracted.
change: Gate value = (net + bank taken + unsold_end − unsold_start) ÷ seconds × 3600, measured in the bots' gate runs with `board.a` 0 (usual prices every day). In I, add only the Yard sale's premium (0.6 of what it pays) and the van's (1/3), and subtract reagents a kg from m̄.

where: 2.12 "The boss" ("While he is in the yard a tagged thing is his: he racks it or cuts it") and "What" (the tag a pure hash of the uid); ruling 10.10
problem: Ruling 10.10 cannot work. While the boss is in the yard, crews may not touch tagged things, and far more arrive than the rack can sell, so the floor fills and loads cannot tip: the yard stalls while the boss is in it and earns less than when he is away. Separately, a tag that is a pure hash of the uid would also tag things below rung 3 and change the measured first hour.
evidence: Farm skips carry 7 things of reuse kinds, demolition skips 4. At share 0.25 and about 39 loads an hour that is about 53 tagged things an hour, plus 7.6 from the drop-off. The rack sells at most refPrice ÷ period = 15 radiators an hour. About 45 an hour (2-3 t) stay on a 4,000 kg floor (floorRoom_kg) that no crew may touch, so it is full inside two hours.
change: One rule, present and away: a tagged thing is the boss's only while he is within reach.sight of it and a slot is free. Otherwise yard hands rack it within their load while a slot is free, and crews cut it when no slot is free. Tags exist only from rung 3. Write L2's 'the ceiling follows I' into 2.12: next visitor at t + 3600 × q ÷ (reuse.shareI × I), with reuse.shareI by rung (first value 0.025, tuned with the van to the 2-5 % band). I is a pure function of assets, so a tick still equals a jump.
ruling: do: one rule, present and away: a tagged thing is the boss's only while he is within sight of it and a slot is free; otherwise yard hands rack it within their load while a slot is free, and crews cut it when no slot is free; tags exist only from rung 3. (It replaces ruling 10.10's 'while he is in the yard a tagged thing is his'.)

where: 2.5.1 (no asFound column), 2.9 the bridge partners' loads, 5.2 check (8), 2.14.7 aim
problem: The bridge partners' loads go against E20 (three fifths of the margin from the yard's work, nothing that needs a tool the player cannot own when the partner opens), and while a loan is open they net a loss. Check (8) cannot see it because it values a whole skip at its best prepared value and at p̄.
evidence: partners.ts defaults asFound to 1. A whole battery from the garage at rung 3, before the lead line: label 0.85 × 15 × 1.80 = §22.95, sold whole §27.00. None of the margin comes from the yard's work, and with an agreement open it nets 27 × 0.8 − 22.95 = −§1.35. The same applies to bushings (bzs before the induction hall), sinks (ssu before the analyser), and clean pipe and fittings. Brass at asFound 0.9 loses after a one-day fall: 0.8 × 0.943 < 0.765.
change: Add `asFound` to 2.5.1. Make the bridge partners' loads from what rung-3 tools improve, or gate `truckBridge` on the analyser and add batteries and bushings to the garage's loads only once the lead line and the induction hall exist. Run check (8) per load, at the plates the partner's gate guarantees, after a one-day fall (prices move at most 5.7 % a day): prepared × (1 − s) × 0.943 ≥ price. The farm passes: 1.378 ≥ 1.326.

where: 2.10.1 ("with four waiting, the next comes the instant one is opened"; "lots.nextAt"), 2.20 ("lots.nextAt = now + period")
problem: The text does not say whether lots are dated in yard seconds or market time, and catch-up after four are waiting has no limit. Lots then pay for absence far beyond the away cap. The migration's nextAt gives a save below rung 3 a backlog when it reaches rung 3. The same question is open for reuse.nextAt, vanAt and the crate's hold date.
evidence: Away 30 h at rung 3 in market time: four lots wait from h12. Each opening brings another while nextAt ≤ now (h12, 15, … 30), so ten lots arrive, about 2.5 h of I, from an absence whose yard ran 6 h.
change: Date lots in yard seconds, so they ride the away cap. At every arrival, nextAt = max(nextAt, t) + period. An opening that leaves three with nextAt ≤ t brings one lot at t and sets nextAt = t + period. nextAt is first set at `backFieldOpen`, not at creation or migration. Say the same for reuse.nextAt, vanAt and crate.since. At the twice-a-day habit this halves the design's '8 lots a day': measure the D4 aim with it.

where: 2.5.3 `out: [GradeId, share][]` (one output list per plate), 2.8 battery breaker and shredder, 5.2 checks
problem: Some plates make output worth less than their input, and the shredder applies the same output shares to every input, so it makes non-ferrous out of light iron. No check refuses either.
evidence: Battery breaker alone: 1.80 → 0.06 × 0.90 + 0.64 × 2.20 − 0.05 × 0.40 = §1.44/kg (−20 %). Routed by default as 'the plate bought last', every battery goes there until the smelter is bought, I falls when the breaker is bought, and its payback price is negative (so the floor). Shredder: light iron yields 8 % zorba and, through the sorter, 1.2 % No.2 copper, §0.41/kg of copper out of a grade worth §0.50 (light iron becomes §1.77/kg through the line).
change: Set pbp p̄ ≥ 2.90 (inference: +5 % on the breaker, the smelter still +71 %), or sell breaker and smelter as one plate, 'Lead line'. Give `out` per input (li → shred 0.95 and residue 0.05; appl and cbody as written). New check (11): every plate and recipe nets at least +5 % at p̄ after reagents, and every plate's ΔI > 0 at its planned moment.

where: 2.14.5 the lender's letter ("P > cash in hand and cash − reserve ≥ d"), LEAD L1 aim, 2.14.7 "finance is the better choice on a quarter to a half of the offers"
problem: For the twice-a-day habit there is no moment at the start of a sitting when the letter can show. It shows only mid-sitting, after other purchases, so L1's 12-of-15 aim depends on the order in which the bots buy, and the 'quarter to a half of offers' band may rest on one or two offers a seed.
evidence: REPORT6 F6: a sitting starts with §162k to §185k in hand, about 6 h of a net I near §25k. A rung-3 plate costs 9 ΔI, so P > cash needs ΔI > 2/3 I. The letter needs 0.2 P + reserve ≤ cash < P at the moment a card opens.
change: Specify that the bots open cards in the goal card's order. Define an offer as a financeable card opening with P > cash after the letter has been seen. Print offers per seed. The band needs at least 3 offers on 13 of 15 seeds; otherwise report it as not measured rather than met.

where: 2.14.5 and 4.3 "Save up (about x)", x = (P − cash) ÷ I
problem: While a loan is open the shown save-up time is about half the real one, because the bank's fifth is taken from gross sales and I is net.
evidence: At the played ratio (sales §1,757 against net §700 a minute), 0.2 × gross is half of net. A card that says 'about 2 h' takes about 4 h until T is repaid.
change: While an agreement is open, x = (P − cash) ÷ (I − bank.share × G), where G is the rated gross an hour (sales before feed) from the same closed form as I.

where: 2.15.4 ("stores pending {product, S, I, at} (one per product)") and 2.15.5 the grant

where: 2.7 Depollution bay ('one elv at a time on its apron (by the forklift, the magnet crane, or tipped within the crane's reach)'); 2.7 Magnet crane ('...and the depollution bay's apron ... and onto the apron'); 2.9 {partner.garage} ('batteries (pbb whole, 15 kg each) ... elv cars' carried as skips 'in rotation', so tipped at the tipping floor); 3.3 note 'Batteries reach the pbb bay as whole things weighed at the platform scale'

Loose lead-acid batteries tipped with wheels and looms onto a floor crack and leak acid. Batteries travel upright in a closed acid-proof box and are stored on a bunded floor. The document itself says pbb is 'never a heap', yet its tip makes a heap first.

ELV fluids and airbags are hazardous waste, handled only on permitted sites'). The first yard's glossary entry 'Depolluted: a car with its fluids, battery, tyres and airbags taken out'. Smallest example: the garage's first skip after the depollution bay holds an elv and six batteries. (2) 2.7 Magnet crane: delete 'and the depollution bay's apron' and 'and onto the apron'; add 'it lifts a car only as a drained shell (cbody)'. (3) 2.9 and 2.10.2 (the tip): 'an elv in a load arrives on the hook-lift's flat body and is set down on an ELV pad (new place, impermeable concrete with a drain, beside the apron, 3 x 5 m) instead of being tipped; the batteries in a load ride in a closed acid-proof box, set down unopened, weighed as one weigh-in and put whole into the battery box; neither goes to the crate'. ruling: do (blocking): an end-of-life car is never tipped from a skip and never lifted by the magnet; it comes on its wheels or on a car transporter to its own pad, is set on the depollution bay's apron by the forklift, and only a depolluted shell goes on; whole batteries come in a closed battery box, never loose in a skip; map, content, art and the partner's loads follow.

Filter dust of any kind is a fine powder kept in closed bags under cover, never in an open bunker.
